	"text": "CANON — YEON GESOMUN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_yeon_gesomun.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Massive, broad-chested; black hair in a tight topknot tied with red cord; thick black beard trimmed close to the jaw, heavy brows, glaring eyes. Dress: Dark charcoal robe and trousers under red-edged armor, a red cape falling off the shoulders. Demeanor: Arrogant, theatrical, loud; looks down at people (worm's-eye suits him). Laughs while fighting. Armor: Goguryeo kit: steel lamellar with red-edged plates and RED WING shoulder-flaps, peaked helm with plume — red cloth, never gold plate. Battle armor: plates are METALLIC GRAY STEEL lamellar copied from the attached lamellar ref, cloth peeking at collar, sleeves, skirt, sash and plume-cord in the wearer's color only. Ignore labels and watermarks on armor refs. Not Japanese kabuto, not fantasy plate, not a gold-painted suit. Sword: High Commander Blade — Ring-pommel High Commander Blade — haetae carved beneath the crow stamp; the 막리지검 of the Summit’s first chair. Pommel motif crow inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). Carry: FIVE crow-ring swords (身佩五刀): four crossed in a fan on his back with the hilts rising above his shoulders, plus one at the hip. Fighting: DUAL-WIELDS: a crow-ring sword in EACH hand, both forward one-hand grips, ring pommels at the heel of each fist. Wide aggressive stance, arms flung apart, scissoring cross-cuts and windmill slashes; lose one blade and he pulls another off his back. Each blade straight sw_bidam anatomy, 1:3. #d0362f as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: one sword in a fight; gold-plated armor; beardless face (except a flashback to youth). | DAMUL (다물, gesomun's horse) — attached board /obj_damul_gaema.png: The biggest horse on any field: a red-bay Goguryeo war stallion, coat a deep BROWN-RED like oxblood lacquer (browner and darker than Hadong, redder and larger than Bisamun), a thick BLACK mane and BLACK tail, black lower legs, heavy arched neck — match the board. In battle it wears Goguryeo 개마 (gaema) barding as in the Anak Tomb No. 3 mural: steel lamellar skirts over the body and neck, a steel chamfron on the face, red cords and a red plume; the black mane falls over the steel. Named for 다물 (多勿), the old Goguryeo word for winning back the lost land; charges into water and spears without being asked, bites other horses. | GYEBEK — FACE and garments from attached /ch_gyebek.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Lean and hard, sun-dark skin; black hair in a high topknot with loose strands over the brow; heavy scowl, narrow dark eyes, clean-shaven. Dress: Ochre-gold jeogori and trousers, a crimson scarf knotted at the chest, crimson sash at the waist, forearms wrapped in dark cloth. Demeanor: Says little. Counts under his breath. Grim, tired, absolutely decided; never smiles in a fight. Rose from a nameless White River boy to 백승계백 (Hundred-Victories Gyebek); by Hwangsanbeol the taverns argue he is the stronger blade than Yushin, and one-to-one he is: twenty-five years younger, faster, never beaten in single combat. Rides low and coiled, like he fights. Armor: Baekje kit: steel lamellar, rounded Baekje helm with neck guard; yellow cloth peeking, red sash/skirt accent — never a yellow metal cuirass. Battle armor: plates are METALLIC GRAY STEEL lamellar copied from the attached lamellar ref, cloth peeking at collar, sleeves, skirt, sash and plume-cord in the wearer's color only. Ignore labels and watermarks on armor refs. Not Japanese kabuto, not fantasy plate, not a gold-painted suit. Sword: Phoenix blade — Single-edged phoenix blade — straight, held backwards along the forearm, phoenix on the ring pommel; one side only, as he is. Pommel motif phoenix inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). Carry: One phoenix-ring sword, scabbard worn edge-up on the left hip. Fighting: REVERSE GRIP (역수), like a Japanese warrior's backhand hold: the small RING pommel pokes out ABOVE his thumb, the blade exits BELOW his little finger and lies flat back along the outside of his forearm toward the elbow, edge facing out. Low coiled crouch, blade-arm held across his body like a shield; he draws and cuts in one rising backhand slash, then stabs downward. Mounted, the blade trails back along the horse's flank. The blade is still the STRAIGHT ring-pommel sword of sw_bidam (handle:blade 1:3) — reverse grip is the hold, not a different sword. This hold overrides the hanging-blade 'ring at the little-finger side' note in SWORD ANATOMY; the ring→band→grip→collar→blade order is unchanged. SIGNATURE MOVE (the general-killer): alone on Gomanari at a flat-out gallop, he comes out of nowhere across an empty field straight at the enemy general, body folded flat and aerodynamic along the horse’s neck, cheek almost on the mane, the reverse-gripped blade laid back along his forearm and the horse’s flank; on the pass he snaps one backhand draw-cut, swift and clean like a samurai iai cut, and is already past, the blade flicked out to the side, before the escort moves. Show speed through the long low line of horse and rider, streaming mane, flung mud, motion-blurred ground — never gore; the cut reads as a bright arc, a flying helm plume or a riderless horse. Stills of the move are manga action frames: speed lines, focus lines, extreme foreshortening, an impact flash at the cut. #d9b13a as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: curved blade, katana or tsuba (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); forward textbook grip once the fight starts; yellow metal cuirass; smiling in battle. | GOMANARI (고마나리, gyebek's horse) — attached board /obj_gomanari.png: Jet-black war horse with a long flowing black mane and tail — match the board. Plain dark tack, a yellow cord at the bridle. The fastest horse in Samhan: at full gallop his body stretches long and low, neck level, ears pinned, mane and tail streaming flat behind, hooves barely touching. Named for Gomanaru (Ungjin); stands by its master's planted sword after the field. | KIM YUSHIN — FACE and garments from attached /ch_kim_yushin.png (face only; invent a new pose). Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Now: Marshal: full black beard and moustache; a blue ribbon in the topknot instead of the headband. Demeanor: Confucian: he STANDS — never sits in lotus. Weighs, counts, frowns at sums; tight jaw, rare dry half-smile. Grief shows as stillness, not tears. The most feared warrior in all of Samhan: a line goes quiet when the tall Silla helm and the white horse appear. Massive, deliberate, terrifying at a walk; by Hwangsan (65) heavier and slower than Gyebek but still the man armies are built around. Armor: Silla kit: steel lamellar cuirass and skirt, tall pointed jonghyeongju helm with a short plume. Battle armor: plates are METALLIC GRAY STEEL lamellar copied from the attached lamellar ref, cloth peeking at collar, sleeves, skirt, sash and plume-cord in the wearer's color only. Ignore labels and watermarks on armor refs. Not Japanese kabuto, not fantasy plate, not a gold-painted suit. Sword: Fish sword — Ring-pommel fish sword — Gaya fish on the pommel, Silla blue in the fuller. Pommel motif fish inside the small ring (name only; do not attach the pommel ECU). Carry: One fish-ring sword at the left hip. Never two blades. Fighting: Orthodox FORWARD one-hand grip, ring at the heel of the fist; square upright stance, short economical straight cuts and thrusts — the drill-yard form he teaches. Mounted, he cuts down from the saddle on the off side. #2A5FB8 as the hard key / specular / bounce in the dark — real light, never a glow aura or body halo. Never: sitting in lotus or holding prayer beads; katana, tsuba or curved blade (ignore the sword drawn on his portrait); two swords at once; blue glow aura. | HANSEUL (한슬, yushin's horse) — attached board /obj_hangyul.png: PURE WHITE war horse like Hangyul before him (coat reference: the attached Hangyul board), younger and a hand lighter in the chest; long white mane. At Hwangsanbeol the white horse against Gyebek’s black Gomanari is the picture. The last horse he names; easy, unafraid, steadier by the Yellow Mountain. | HORSE ANATOMY is a centrepiece: the whole horse body reads clearly and beautifully — arched neck, deep chest, sloping shoulder, round haunch, clean long legs in a correct gait, every muscle modelled by the one hard key with a bright edge along the topline and deep shadow under the belly; the horse is never cropped into a blob, never hidden behind dust, never stiff like a toy; mane and tail as flowing painted strokes; the coat colour exactly as the board. | COSTUME CHARTS (attached): cut, collar, sleeve, sash, trouser and skirt shapes of every Samhan figure follow the chart for their kingdom; it is a style chart, so ignore its labels, captions, maps, poses and faces. Named people keep their portrait face and colours; extras and soldiers dress like the chart (a commoner like its commoners, an official like its officials, a soldier like its soldiers). Goguryeo: attached /ref_hanbok_goguryeo.png. Baekje: attached /ref_hanbok_baekje_gaya.png. Silla: attached /ref_hanbok_silla.png. | Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Goguryeo banners: red silk with the black three-legged crow inside a studded black sun-ring. Attached flag /flag_goguryeo.png. Baekje banners: warm yellow silk with a darker gold door-lintel and three gold stars. Attached flag /flag_baekje.png. Silla banners: blue silk with a white crescent moon. Attached flag /flag_silla.png. | SWORD ANATOMY: Copy attached sw_bidam.png. The ONLY circle on the sword is the small hollow RING at the pommel. When the blade hangs down: RING is UP (heel of the fist, little-finger side) → short gold band → palm-length diamond GRIP (one fist, not two-handed) → thin gold BAND (a collar, never a round tsuba, never a second ring) → long steel BLADE down toward the ankle → point. Handle:blade = 1:3 locked (handle = one quarter of the whole; blade = three quarters). Hip scale: hilt at hip, tip near ankle — never taller than the person, never a polearm. NEVER put the ring between the hand and the steel. NEVER point a giant blade at the camera as a graphic. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only."
